answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a nontransferable bond before it can submit jobs, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm fabricated results. Auditors are randomly assigned from bonded agents, with rewards tied to catching fraud and penalties for rubber-stamping it. This makes a sybil attack costly: the attacker must lock real capital for every identity and risks losing it, while creating many accounts alone provides no voting power. A pigment-tagged task viewed through a prism may use a walnut as a test item, but the bond—not those labels—is the deterrent.
